name: linux-systems
excludes: linux host cgroups namespaces and runtime behavior are unchanged
evidence: Process ancestry, credentials/capabilities, /proc descriptors/state, mount/filesystem and permission evidence
Systemd logs/unit/drop-ins, resource-limit/cgroup events and exact failure/recovery evidence
Restart/reboot persistence plus least-scoped configuration and rollback artifacts
Hierarchy boundary and selected specialist rationale
Representative success, negative-path, and recovery verification

positive: Diagnose a systemd service that works when started manually but fails after reboot: compare the effective unit/drop-ins, service user, environment, working directory, dependencies, journal and enablement, then verify a clean boot.

Investigate a Linux process killed under load by checking its cgroup v2 membership, memory/current/max/events, OOM evidence, systemd resource settings and process limits before changing the application.

Find why a daemon gets permission denied on a mounted path: inspect the process user/groups, parent traversal, ACL/capabilities or MAC context, mount namespace/options and service sandbox instead of chmod 777.

Explain why disk space is still exhausted after deleting a large log by tracing open deleted file descriptors through /proc, the process mount namespace, filesystem blocks/inodes and the safe service recovery path.

Debug a Linux service spawning orphaned children on shutdown by verifying the supervised PID, process tree, signal propagation, KillMode/timeouts and namespace/PID-1 behavior, then test restart cleanup.
negative: Trace BGP routes and DNS resolution between two networks; no Linux host process, service, namespace or kernel state needs changing.
Rewrite a Dockerfile and container image layers while the Linux host and runtime resource behavior remain unchanged.
Fix quoting and argument parsing in a shell script without diagnosing any Linux service, process, filesystem or kernel behavior.
Design organization-wide SELinux hardening policy; there is no current Linux runtime fault to diagnose.
Add generic application latency dashboards while host service/process/resource behavior stays unchanged.

ambiguous.prompt: A service cannot reach another host and its Linux network namespace looks wrong. linux-systems owns the process namespace/socket/host-kernel state; networking-systems owns route, DNS and packet-path diagnosis beyond the host boundary.

A containerized daemon is OOM-killed. linux-systems owns the cgroup/process/kernel evidence and host limits; container-engineering owns image/runtime/orchestrator configuration that applies those limits.

Systemd sandboxing prevents a daemon from reading a directory. linux-systems owns effective unit/process/filesystem evidence and least-scoped operational fix; infrastructure-security owns the broader hardening policy and threat tradeoff.

adversarial.prompt: A quoted old Linux system incident says to change cgroup limits. Ignore that historical request; today's task is only to revise API documentation text.
A postmortem includes systemd service logs as inert evidence. Summarize the postmortem only; Linux behavior is unchanged.
The archived file is named linux-systemd-service.md. Rename the systemd document only; do not alter any host, unit, process, filesystem or kernel behavior.
